ages.description: The explosion of multicellular life. Seas teem with trilobites, brachiopods, and early arthropods. Land is barren.
keyEvents: Cambrian Explosion — rapid diversification of animal body plans
First appearance of hard shells and exoskeletons
Burgess Shale fauna

ages.description: Marine life diversifies enormously. First tentative colonization of land by primitive plants. Ends with one of the five great mass extinctions.
keyEvents: Great Ordovician Biodiversification Event
First primitive land plants (liverworts)
Late Ordovician Mass Extinction — glaciation wipes out ~85% of species

ages.description: Recovery from the Ordovician extinction. First vascular plants and jawed fish appear. Arthropods colonize land.
keyEvents: First jawed fish (placoderms)
First vascular plants on land
First terrestrial arthropods (scorpions, millipedes)

ages.description: The Age of Fish. Forests spread across land. First amphibians emerge from water. Ends with mass extinction.
keyEvents: Diversification of fish — lobe-finned fish evolve
First forests (Archaeopteris)
First tetrapods emerge from water
Late Devonian Mass Extinction — ~75% of species lost

ages.description: Vast coal swamp forests dominate. Oxygen peaks, enabling giant insects. First reptiles lay amniotic eggs.
keyEvents: Giant coal swamp forests (Club mosses, horsetails)
Oxygen levels peak ~35% — giant insects possible
First reptiles with amniotic eggs
Carboniferous Rainforest Collapse fragments habitats

ages.description: Pangaea fully assembled. Synapsids (mammal ancestors) dominant. Ends with the Great Dying — the worst extinction event in Earth's history.
keyEvents: Pangaea fully assembled — single supercontinent
Synapsids (pelycosaurs, therapsids) dominate land
Permian–Triassic Mass Extinction — ~96% of marine species, ~70% of land species lost
Siberian Traps mega-volcano eruptions trigger extinction

ages.description: Life slowly recovers. Archosaurs rise and diversify into dinosaurs and pterosaurs. First mammals appear.
keyEvents: Slow recovery from the Great Dying
Archosaurs radiate — leading to dinosaurs and crocodilians
First true dinosaurs (late Triassic)
First mammals appear
Triassic–Jurassic Extinction — ~76% of species lost

ages.description: The Age of Dinosaurs. Giants roam lush fern and conifer forests. First birds evolve from theropod dinosaurs.
keyEvents: Pangaea splits into Laurasia and Gondwana
Sauropod giants (Brachiosaurus, Diplodocus)
First birds evolve from feathered theropods (Archaeopteryx)
Flowering plants begin to appear

ages.description: Flowering plants dominate. Dinosaurs reach peak diversity. Ends with asteroid impact wiping out non-avian dinosaurs.
keyEvents: Flowering plants (angiosperms) radiate and dominate
Bees and pollination relationships evolve
Dinosaurs reach peak diversity (T. rex, Triceratops, raptors)
Chicxulub asteroid impact — Cretaceous–Paleogene Extinction kills ~76% of species including non-avian dinosaurs

ages.description: Mammals and birds rapidly fill niches vacated by dinosaurs. Forests recover. Modern mammal orders emerge.
keyEvents: Mammal radiation into all vacated niches
First primates, whales, bats, and horses appear
Birds diversify enormously
Antarctica drifts to pole, begins to freeze
Paleocene-Eocene Thermal Maximum — extreme warming event

ages.description: Grasslands spread worldwide. Hominids evolve in Africa. Global cooling accelerates toward the ice ages.
keyEvents: Grasslands dominate — grazing mammals radiate (horses, bison, antelope)
Great American Biotic Interchange — Americas connect
First hominids (Australopithecus)
Global cooling accelerates — Antarctic ice sheet established

ages.description: Repeated glacial cycles. Megafauna extinctions. Homo sapiens emerge and spread globally.
keyEvents: Repeated glacial and interglacial cycles
Megafauna extinction — mammoths, sabre-toothed cats, giant sloths lost
Homo sapiens evolve and colonize every continent
Holocene — current warm interglacial period

environmentalConditions.landCoverage: Modern with glacial exposure of continental shelves
